scenario_identification.reasoning: The scenario name resolves to three cached items, all of which are TARGET-side debuffs: 'mandate' = Imperial Mandate (id 4005, 'Command' = 7% Vulnerable amp), 'abyssal' = Abyssal Mask (id 8020, 'Unmake' = 12% increased magic damage taken), 'curse' = Bloodletter's Curse (id 8010, 'Vile Decay' = up to 30% magic-resist reduction). All three are confirmed present and non-stale in data/staleness.json. 'roster' = a coupled multi-participant fight, so breakdown[1] is the SECOND participant in the roster, i.e. not the item owner.
scenario_identification.limitation: The scenario's input tuple (champions, levels, item assignment per roster slot, fight window) lives in scripts/golden_snapshot.py, which this runbook forbids reading, and it is not mirrored anywhere under data/ (grepped: practice-corpus/scenarios.json, worklists/*, champion-audit/*, wiki-atoms/* -- zero hits for the scenario id or for these item names in any scenario context). The absolute value therefore cannot be reconstructed from first principles; what CAN be computed exactly from the cached wiki text is the multiplicative structure the leaf must obey, and the three candidate values are fully discriminated by it.

independent_computation.step_1_governing_rule: S1 and S2 are both debuffs on the TARGET and both say the amplification applies to damage 'from all sources'. In a coupled roster this means every participant's damage into that target is amplified, not only the item owner's. S3 likewise is a resistance debuff on the target, visible to every attacker. Therefore breakdown[1] -- a roster member that does not own the items -- MUST receive these amplifications. Any model that scopes them to the owner understates breakdown[1]'s outgoing_damage_before_death.
independent_computation.step_2_amp_vs_pen: S1 says 'receive 12% increased magic damage', i.e. a post-mitigation damage-taken multiplier of 1.12 on the magic sub-total. Per S5 that is categorically NOT 12% percent magic penetration (a resistance operator R <- max(0, 0.88R) applied before S4's m(R)). The two give different numbers for every R > 0; only the amplifier form matches the quoted text.
independent_computation.step_3_linearity: By S6, mitigation is linear in raw damage at fixed R, so a target-side amplifier factors out of a damage sub-total: total = D_nonmagic + D_magic * A, with A the product of the applicable amplifiers. The leaf is the cumulative-damage functional of S7, i.e. a sum of such events, so the same factorization holds for the leaf.

step_4_ladder_identity.observation: The three candidate values form an exact multiplicative ladder on the C3 tip:
step_4_ladder_identity.conclusion: The leaf differs between versions only by a uniform factor of 1.00 / 1.03 / 1.06 applied to a fixed underlying event ledger. Because an amplifier factors out (step 3), the modeled amplification of breakdown[1]'s total went 0% (C3 tip) -> +3% (frozen baseline) -> +6% (new). A resistance-side explanation is ruled out: with a fixed raw ledger, successive equal reductions of R give an INCREASING sequence of ratios (m(R) is convex in R, S4/math-foundations 2.3), whereas the observed ratios DECREASE (1.02994 then 1.02919) -- the signature of a linear-in-amplifier ladder, not a resistance ladder.

step_5_solve_for_the_magic_share.equation: new = old * (1 - f + f*1.12) = old * (1 + 0.12 f), where f = magic share of breakdown[1]'s outgoing damage
step_5_solve_for_the_magic_share.result: f = 0.500 to four significant figures. The new value is exactly the C3 tip with Abyssal Mask's sourced 12% magic amplification (S1) applied to a breakdown[1] whose outgoing damage is half magic -- 1 + 0.12*0.5 = 1.06 exactly.

step_6_discriminate_the_alternatives.note: All evaluated at the same f = 0.5 implied by step 5, against the same C3 event ledger.
step_6_discriminate_the_alternatives.reading: 838.3 corresponds to the amplification being absent from a participant that does not own the item -- contradicted by S1's 'from all sources'. 863.4 reproduces exactly either the stale half-magnitude (6%) reading or the penetration mis-model of S1 at a plausible post-Vile-Decay MR (~80), both contradicted by S1's literal '12% increased magic damage' and by S5's separation of penetration from amplification. 888.6 is the unique value consistent with the quoted 12% magic-damage amplifier applied, per 'from all sources', to a roster participant that does not own Abyssal Mask. It is also the multiplicative-composition value: had the engine instead added the 12% and the 7% Vulnerable amp into one 19% bucket, the leaf would read 885.3, which it does not.

confidence_and_caveats: HIGH on the mechanism and the direction: S1 and S2 both say 'from all sources', which is a target-side amplification that a coupled roster must extend to every participant; the change moves breakdown[1] upward, as required.

HIGH on the magnitude being the sourced 12% (not a half-strength 6% and not a penetration mis-model): the ladder identity fixes the modeled amplification to exactly +6.00% of the total, and the implied magic share solves to f = 0.50002 -- i.e. 12% applied to exactly half the participant's outgoing damage. The frozen baseline's +3.00% is exactly half that, the signature of a halved constant (or of the penetration mis-model, which lands on the same 1.030 at MR ~= 80).

RESIDUAL RISK: I could not read the scenario's input tuple (it lives in scripts/, out of scope for this runbook, and is not mirrored under data/), so f = 0.5 is solved FROM the deltas rather than verified independently. If breakdown[1]'s outgoing damage were in fact 100% magic, the sourced 12% would demand 938.9 and all three candidates would be wrong. I judge that unlikely: a 100%-magic participant would make the frozen baseline a 6%/3% pair with no sourced counterpart at all, whereas f = 0.5 makes the new value land on the sourced 12% exactly and the baseline on exactly half of it.

Vile Decay (S3) and the Vulnerable mark (S2) are unchanged by this leaf's delta: a Vile Decay stack change would move the leaf on the resistance side, which the convexity argument in step 4 rules out, and the 7% Vulnerable amp would give 897.0 on the full total or 867.6 on the magic half -- neither matches.
